title: Issue #121: Architecture: AI Compute Mining + independent PoS network security + ATC settlement
content:
State: open

## Objective

Define **Variant A: AI Mining + Proof of Stake (PoS)** as the target architecture for A-TownChain.

- AI miners perform useful, externally executed compute jobs and are paid in ATC after acceptance.
- Stakers/validators secure blockchain consensus independently of AI job execution.
- ATC is the common settlement asset for compute payments, transaction fees, and protocol-defined validator rewards.
- AI job success MUST NOT itself grant consensus authority or determine canonical chain state.

This issue is an architecture/specification task only. It does not claim that the mechanisms are implemented or verified.

## Canonical ownership / SSOT

- `a-townchain`: canonical blockchain core, consensus, transaction processing, and economic settlement implementation.
- `a-townchain/components/algorithm`: canonical consensus/algorithm implementation.
- `a-townchain/components/vm`: canonical deterministic ATC-VM; no off-chain AI execution inside consensus execution.
- `aurora-ai`: AI orchestration and AI service integration only; no consensus authority.
- `a-townchain-ecosystem`: cross-repository architecture, contracts, integration requirements, compliance and evidence coordination only; do not duplicate component implementations here.

Compute-worker/marketplace implementation ownership must be resolved against the active repository inventory before implementation; do not create a competing SSOT.

## Target flow

1. A user submits a compute job and commits to an ATC-denominated budget.
2. A scheduler assigns work to an eligible compute provider.
3. The provider executes the job outside deterministic consensus execution.
4. The result is validated under a versioned task-specific verification policy (e.g. deterministic recomputation, redundant execution, benchmark/constraint checks, or cryptographic proof where appropriate).
5. A settlement transaction releases the agreed ATC payment only after the acceptance policy succeeds.
6. PoS validators independently validate blocks and finalize state according to the canonical consensus rules.
7. Transaction fees and validator rewards are accounted for separately from compute-job payments.

## Required protocol contracts

### AI compute mining
- Versioned job schema, task class, model/runtime/artifact digests, inputs/data access policy, resource limits, deadline, cancellation and retry semantics.
- Explicit result acceptance policy per task class; no generic claim that every AI result is objectively verifiable.
- Anti-replay, duplicate-work, Sybil/fraud and collusion mitigations.
- Deterministic accounting for accepted work, partial completion, timeout, failure, disputes and refunds.
- Privacy, licensing and data-retention constraints for job inputs and outputs.
- Compute rewards funded by the user's escrowed payment or an explicitly budgeted protocol source.

### Independent PoS security
- Validator eligibility, stake accounting, selection, block proposal/attestation, quorum/finality, downtime behavior, unbonding and slashing rules.
- Consensus safety and liveness must not depend on AI-job availability or output quality.
- AI providers do not gain validator privileges by completing compute jobs; any dual role must satisfy both independent role contracts.
- Prevent duplicate reward claims and define deterministic handling of conflicting settlements.

### ATC economics and settlement
- Keep user-funded compute payments, transaction fees, validator rewards and issuance as separate accounting categories.
- Define fee calculation, fee recipient/burn/treasury policy, reward source, rounding, failure semantics and replay protection.
- Respect the existing 360,000,000 ATC maximum supply and 18 decimal places; any reward proposal must reconcile with the canonical issuance schedule and may not silently introduce uncapped issuance.
- Do not assume a fee split, reward rate, emission schedule or slashing percentage until specified and reviewed.

## Security boundaries

- Compute execution is off-chain; only bounded, validated settlement/state transitions enter the canonical chain.
- Aurora AI can propose and orchestrate jobs but cannot authorize privileged state changes by model output alone.
- ATC-VM remains deterministic and resource-bounded.
- Fail closed when task policy, result evidence, authorization, budget, or settlement inputs are missing or invalid.
- No weakening of existing CI/security gates and no automatic merge.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Architecture explicitly documents AI mining and PoS as independent mechanisms.
- [ ] Canonical repository ownership and cross-repository API/ABI contracts are recorded.
- [ ] Job lifecycle and result acceptance policy are specified by task class.
- [ ] ATC settlement accounting distinguishes compute payments, fees, validator rewards and issuance.
- [ ] Supply cap and existing tokenomics are reconciled without unsupported assumptions.
- [ ] Threat model covers fraudulent results, collusion, Sybil attacks, replay, double payment, validator attacks and data leakage.
- [ ] Unit, integration, adversarial and deterministic-settlement test plans are defined.
- [ ] Implementation status is reported separately as SPECIFIED / IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / CI_VERIFIED / INTEGRATED / E2E_VERIFIED.
- [ ] Any VERIFIED claim is tied to an exact commit SHA and terminal Run → Job → Step → exit/log evidence.

## Non-goals

- Do not turn useful AI work into a consensus mechanism in this variant.
- Do not execute arbitrary AI workloads inside ATC-VM or validator consensus paths.
- Do not introduce new token issuance or fixed reward percentages without a reviewed economic specification.
- Do not merge implementation changes as part of this architecture issue.
